dash.title: Talent strategy dashboard
dash.subtitleHr: {{cycle}} · Retention, succession and development of key talent across the plant
dash.scopeNoteManager: Covers your team and your line; Supervisors below you count only once they have submitted.
dash.noData: No data in the current scope.

completion.def: Key talent reviews already submitted to HR (including confirmed and locked).
completion.formula: Key talent submitted or later ÷ all key talent
completion.use: If it lags, open Review progress to see which teams have not submitted. Other measures are only representative once completion is high.

key.def: People a Supervisor marked as key talent this cycle.
key.formula: Number of key talent; share = key talent ÷ people in scope
key.use: The share is a reference, never a target. Use it to check that departments nominate consistently and raise outliers in calibration.

alert.def: People in a critical role who are rated high retention risk.
alert.formula: Critical role = yes and retention risk = High
alert.use: Losing them hits the business immediately. Agree an individual retention action with the Supervisor and HRBP within two weeks.

ready.def: Share of critical roles with at least one successor who could step in now.
ready.formula: Critical roles with a Ready Now successor ÷ all critical roles
ready.use: Low coverage means an opening is likely filled from outside or stays vacant. Start with the Succession gaps list.

talk.def: Key talent whose Supervisor ticked 'career goals not yet discussed'.
talk.use: A 15-minute career conversation is the cheapest retention action. Start with medium and high risk.

health.def: Four core measures per department, compared with the overall value of the current filter.
health.formula: Flagged when 10 or more points worse than overall.
health.use: Start with the department with the most flags, then open the other sections for the reasons. This compares departments, not Supervisors.

headcount.t: Headcount and key talent by department
headcount.def: People in review scope per department and how many of them are key talent.
headcount.formula: Dark = key talent; light = others in scope; percentage = key talent ÷ people in scope
headcount.use: Check whether key talent sits in a few departments. Clear differences in share are worth a consistency check.

gender.q: Do women reach the key talent list at the same rate?
gender.def: Share of women among key talent, compared with their share of everyone in scope.
gender.formula: Female key talent ÷ key talent vs. women ÷ people in scope. Hidden under five people so nobody can be identified.
gender.use: A gap of five points or more is worth checking nomination criteria.

tenure.q: At what career stage is our key talent?
tenure.def: Distribution of key talent and of everyone in scope across tenure bands.
tenure.formula: People in each band ÷ people in that group
tenure.use: Concentrated in senior bands: knowledge-transfer and retirement risk. In junior bands: longer development, more coaching needed.

riskMap.def: Key talent split by retention risk (high, medium, low) and by whether they hold a critical role.
riskMap.formula: Each cell = number of people; click for the list
riskMap.use: Handle high risk × critical role first, then medium risk × critical role.

reasons.def: Reasons Supervisors ticked for medium and high risk people (several allowed).
reasons.formula: People with the reason ÷ medium and high risk people
reasons.use: When reasons cluster, a policy fix (pay, career paths, workload) beats one-by-one retention.

poach.def: High retention risk and already ready for their next role.
poach.formula: Retention risk = High and next-role readiness = Ready Now
poach.use: Ready but without an opportunity. Discuss promotion, rotation or a bigger scope first.

talkRisk.q: Who should we talk to this week?
talkRisk.def: Medium or high retention risk, and the Supervisor has not discussed career goals with them.
talkRisk.formula: Retention risk = Medium or High, and 'not yet discussed' ticked
talkRisk.use: Hold a 15-minute career conversation within two weeks.

benchDept.q: If a critical role opened tomorrow, who would step in?
benchDept.def: Each critical role, grouped by the readiness of its best successor.
benchDept.formula: Ready now; 1–2 years; long-range = 3+ years or emergency cover only; none = no successor or to be hired (TBH)
benchDept.use: Red roles have nobody today. Amber plus red is the two-year succession gap.

uncovered.q: Which critical roles have nobody within two years?
uncovered.def: Critical roles where no successor could take over within two years (long-range, emergency cover, TBH or none).
uncovered.formula: Critical role and best successor is 3+ years, emergency cover or none
uncovered.use: Name a successor first; where nobody exists internally, plan hiring early.

coverage.q: Every critical role at a glance
coverage.def: One tile per critical role, colored by best successor readiness, grouped by department.
coverage.formula: Colors as in Bench strength by department
coverage.use: See where gaps cluster. Select a tile for the holder and successors.

concentration.q: Is someone the backup for several roles?
concentration.def: The same person named as successor for two or more critical roles.
concentration.formula: Roles per named successor, two or more only
concentration.use: One person can fill only one role, so real coverage is lower than it looks. Find a second candidate. HR only.

external.def: Share of successor slots that are external candidates or to be hired (TBH).
external.formula: External and TBH ÷ all successor slots
external.use: Higher means more reliance on hiring and more room to grow internal talent.

fragile.def: The near-term successor (ready now or 1–2 years) of a critical role is themselves at medium or high risk.
fragile.formula: Near-term successor with retention risk Medium or High
fragile.use: Both could leave together. Retaining the successor protects two roles.

pipeline.q: How many are ready to step up?
pipeline.def: Readiness of key talent for their next role. With several next roles, the nearest counts.
pipeline.formula: People at each readiness ÷ key talent with a next role
pipeline.use: Ready people without an opportunity become a retention risk.

mobility.def: Key talent's openness to moving to another department, site or location.
mobility.formula: People per option ÷ key talent who answered
mobility.use: People open to moving soon are the first internal source for openings.

mix.q: Do plans build skills on the job, or only in class?
mix.def: Actual share of development actions by type, against the 70/20/10 reference.
mix.formula: Actions of each type ÷ actions with a type
mix.use: A high share of courses (10%) means plans lack real assignments. The reference is not a target.

checkpoints.def: Development goals falling due in each month.
checkpoints.use: A month before a peak, HR reminds Supervisors to prepare follow-ups.

pbm.q: What are our common strengths and gaps?
pbm.def: How often each Our Values item was named as a strength and as an improvement area.
pbm.formula: Mentions per value (left: improvement, right: strength)
pbm.use: Improvement areas many people share are good topics for a group workshop.

planComplete.def: Share of key talent whose development plan has every required field.
planComplete.formula: Key talent with a complete plan ÷ all key talent
planComplete.use: Incomplete plans cannot be tracked. Ask Supervisors to add actions, dates and how progress is checked.

story.title: What stands out
story.subtitle: Built automatically from the current filter. Every number opens the list.
story.none: Nothing stands out in the current scope.
story.riskHotspot: {{pct}} of key talent in {{dept}} is at medium or high risk, well above overall ({{overall}}).
story.riskHotspotAct: Next: review the reasons with that department's Supervisors
story.uncovered: {{count}} of {{critical}} critical roles have nobody who could take over within two years.
story.uncoveredAct: Next: name successors or plan hiring early
story.concentration: {{name}} is named successor for {{roles}} roles, so real coverage is lower than it looks.
story.concentrationAct: Next: find a second candidate for those roles
story.talkGap: {{count}} people at medium or high risk have not had a career conversation.
story.talkGapAct: Next: hold a 15-minute career conversation within two weeks

bench.noConcentration: Nobody is named for more than one role.

act.title: Action list
act.subtitle: Turns the review into this month's to-dos. Each item is a conversation to have, not a judgement of anyone. Cross-team results are HR only.

talk.why: Medium or high risk, and nobody has discussed their career with them.
talk.next: Supervisor holds a 15-minute conversation within two weeks

fragile.why: The successor may leave too, opening two roles at once.
fragile.next: Add the successor to retention actions, or name a second candidate

hidden.t: Check potential that may be missed
hidden.why: Other Supervisors see them as a near-term successor, but their own Supervisor did not list them as key talent.
hidden.next: Confirm in calibration whether to add them

internal.why: These roles lack successors, and someone's stated next step is exactly this job.
internal.next: Talk to these colleagues before opening the role

calibrate.t: Ask one more question in calibration
calibrate.why: These teams' entries follow a pattern (all low risk, identical readiness) worth confirming.
calibrate.next: HRBP checks the basis for the entries in the discussion

act.none: Nothing to act on right now.

ai.notice: AI analysis sends review content to the Anthropic API for processing
ai.managerNote: AI only makes suggestions and never writes to your forms. Use your own judgment.

err.demo_mode: Demo mode does not call AI. It works once the backend is connected.
